collection.credit:
CHATGPT-WRITTEN EVENTS — WITH LORSIEAB2 CREATIVE DIRECTION
* V6–V8 additional VV1–VV5 event prose, variants and codas:
  ChatGPT, with Lorsieab2's canon guidance, character preferences,
  requests for emotional complexity and patcher constraints.

ledger.text: The village gains a little Tech.

ledger.why: the Research or Devotion effects on the coda page
safety note: the parent is never cast (text only); Isolans are never cast; the event has no harmful effect

items.text: a difficult harvest when neighbors shared the little food they had
the first time two stubborn villagers learned to work together
a child who made an awful carving and insisted it was a masterpiece
an old celebration whose songs are nearly forgotten
a misunderstanding between the village and Isolan neighbors that ended with an unexpected act of kindness
a beloved teacher who always said, "Try again tomorrow"
a grand expedition that was, in truth, a very long walk to find a lost goat
The box is closed and returned to its shelf. Tomorrow, another child may ask about it.
The villagers begin collecting stories from willing elders, carefully marking what is remembered and what is uncertain.
The baby falls asleep. The adults continue talking in whispers.
The child decides that (child.he/she) would like to become old someday, if only to own a box full of mysterious objects.
The elder laughs at an old mistake and says, "I was young once, too."

box.name: The old box
box.text:
The village's oldest (elder.woman/man), (Elder), has been sorting through an old wooden box. Inside is {a worn carving|a faded scrap of cloth|a smooth pebble|a tiny toy|a carefully folded note}. A child, (Child), asks why anyone would bother keeping such an ordinary object.
"Ordinary?" (Elder) says. "This belonged to {a dear friend|my mother|a child I once cared for|someone who taught me to build}."

l_app.text: Nearby, an apprentice pauses to listen.

l_mb.text: Nearby, a Master Builder pauses to listen.

l_mom.text: Nearby, a nursing mother pauses to listen. The parent gently rocks (mom.his/her) baby, who seems far more interested in chewing the edge of a blanket than in history.

l_dad.text: Nearby, a father pauses to listen. The parent gently rocks (dad.his/her) baby, who seems far more interested in chewing the edge of a blanket than in history.

memory.text: The elder tells the story of {A}.

b1.text: The child asks a hundred questions. The elder answers ninety-nine, then admits (elder.he/she) has forgotten the last answer.

b2.text: The apprentice realizes that the object's odd shape records an ingenious building technique.

b3.text: The parent shares a memory from {PARENT} own childhood, and the baby chooses that exact moment to spit up on the family keepsake. The object is cleaned; the story survives.

b4.text: An Isolan visitor recognizes the same song or design from (isolan.his/her) community. The two compare versions without insisting one is superior.

b5.text: The child is disappointed that the story contains no monsters, treasure, or heroic battles. The elder promises that ordinary people are allowed to be interesting too.

b6.text: The elder forgets an important detail. Rather than invent an answer, the villagers decide to ask someone else who might remember.

b7.text: The child offers the elder a new, crooked little carving to add to the box. The elder accepts it with surprising solemnity.
